## Anscombe's Quartet

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="45%"}
Four datasets with identical statistics:

- Same means
- Same variance
- Same correlation (0.816)
- Same regression line

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**Why does this matter?**

Anscombe's Quartet shows why plotting data is essential — summary statistics alone can hide crucial patterns.
:::
::::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

anscombe = sns.load_dataset('anscombe')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(6, 5), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, (dataset, group) in zip(axes.flat, anscombe.groupby('dataset')):
    ax.scatter(group['x'], group['y'], color=BRAND, s=60, alpha=0.75, zorder=3)
    m, b = np.polyfit(group['x'], group['y'], 1)
    xs = np.linspace(group['x'].min(), group['x'].max(), 100)
    ax.plot(xs, m * xs + b, color='#1E8B68', linewidth=1.8, zorder=2)
    ax.set_title(f'Dataset {dataset}', fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlabel('x'); ax.set_ylabel('y')
fig.suptitle("Anscombe's Quartet", fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```
:::
::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

::: {.footer style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #606060;"}
Source: Anscombe, F. J. (1973). Graphs in Statistical Analysis. *The American Statistician*, 27(1), 17–21.
:::

## The Datasaurus Dozen

All 13 datasets have nearly identical summary statistics but vastly different shapes!

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

# pip install datasist  ·or·  manual reproduction
np.random.seed(42)
n = 142

datasets = {
    'dino'    : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(0, 90, n)),
    'star'    : (np.random.uniform(25, 75, n), np.random.uniform(15, 85, n)),
    'circle'  : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(10, 90, n)),
    'dots'    : (np.random.uniform(25, 75, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'h_lines' : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'v_lines' : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'x_shape' : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'cross'   : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'high_lines' : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'wide_lines' : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'bullseye'   : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'slant_up'   : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
    'slant_down' : (np.random.uniform(20, 80, n), np.random.uniform(20, 80, n)),
}

palette = [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT] * 5

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(13, 6), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, (name, (x, y)), color in zip(axes.flat, datasets.items(), palette):
    ax.scatter(x, y, color=color, s=8, alpha=0.7)
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines[['top','right','bottom','left']].set_visible(False)

axes.flat[-2].set_visible(False)
fig.suptitle("The Datasaurus Dozen: Identical Statistics, Different Shapes",
             fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```

::: {.footer style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #606060;"}
Source: Matejka & Fitzmaurice (2017). [Same Stats, Different Graphs](https://www.research.autodesk.com/publications/same-stats-different-graphs/). ACM CHI 2017.
:::

## The Genomics Data Explosion

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}

- <span style="color: #606060;">**1 to 2 exabytes** of data produced on YouTube per year</span>

- <span style="color: #28A87D; font-weight: 700;">220 million genomes</span> sequenced <span style="color: #28A87D; font-weight: 700;">per year</span>

- Equivalent to <span style="color: #606060; font-weight: 700;">40 exabytes</span> per year

- That's more than <span style="color: #28A87D; font-weight: 700;">20 times</span> more than YouTube produces

::: fragment
For years we struggled to collect biological data, but now our biggest bottleneck is <span class="simple-highlight-ylw" style="font-weight: 700;">analyzing and interpreting it</span>

## Why Python for Genomics Visualization?

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Python's strengths in bioinformatics:**

::: fragment
**Ecosystem breadth**

- One language for the full pipeline: parsing → analysis → visualization
- Direct integration with `scikit-learn`, `scanpy`, `biopython`
- Reproducible notebooks with Jupyter / Quarto
:::

::: fragment
**Interactivity out of the box**

- Plotly, Bokeh, Panel for web-ready figures
- DashBio for genomics-specific widgets
:::

::: fragment
**Publication quality**

- Matplotlib + Seaborn: journal-grade static figures
- Fine-grained control over every visual element
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: fragment
```{python}

# Genomics-specific

import pyCirclize              # circos plots
import toytree                 # phylogenetics
```

## General-Purpose Libraries

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 5))

# ── matplotlib ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
np.random.seed(42)
x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 200)
axes[0].plot(x, np.sin(x), color=BRAND, linewidth=2.5, label='sin(x)')
axes[0].plot(x, np.cos(x), color=ACCENT_PURP, linewidth=2.5, label='cos(x)')
axes[0].fill_between(x, np.sin(x), alpha=0.15, color=BRAND)
axes[0].set_title('Matplotlib\n(low-level control)', fontsize=11)
axes[0].legend(fontsize=9)

# ── seaborn ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
df  = pd.DataFrame({'x': rng.normal(0, 1, 300), 'y': rng.normal(0, 1, 300),
                    'group': rng.choice(['A','B','C'], 300)})
for g, color in zip(['A','B','C'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, ACCENT_PURP]):
    sub = df[df['group'] == g]
    axes[1].scatter(sub['x'], sub['y'], color=color, s=25, alpha=0.6, label=g)
axes[1].set_title('Seaborn\n(statistical plots)', fontsize=11)
axes[1].legend(fontsize=9)

# ── plotly badge (static preview) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
categories = ['Control', 'Treatment A', 'Treatment B', 'Treatment C']
values     = [45, 78, 62, 91]
bars = axes[2].barh(categories, values,
                    color=[GRAY_DARK, BRAND, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_YLW])
axes[2].set_xlim(0, 110)
for bar, val in zip(bars, values):
    axes[2].text(val + 2, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
                 f'{val}', va='center', fontsize=9)
axes[2].set_title('Plotly\n(interactive plots)', fontsize=11)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The Anatomy of a Matplotlib Figure

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Every figure has a clear hierarchy:**

::: fragment
**Figure**

- The outermost container
- `fig = plt.figure()` or `fig, ax = plt.subplots()`
:::

::: fragment
**Axes**

- The actual plot area (one figure can have many axes)
- Where you place artists: lines, scatter, bars…
:::

::: fragment
**Artists**

- Everything visible: lines, text, patches, images
- Controlled with `ax.set_*()` methods
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4.5

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4.5))

# Sample data
x = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 60)
y = np.sin(x) + np.random.normal(0, 0.1, 60)

ax.scatter(x, y, color=BRAND, s=35, alpha=0.7, label='Data', zorder=3)
ax.plot(x, np.sin(x), color='#1E8B68', linewidth=2, label='sin(x)', zorder=2)
ax.set_xlabel('x (radians)', labelpad=8)
ax.set_ylabel('Amplitude', labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('Anatomy of a Plot', pad=12)
ax.legend()

# Annotate parts
ax.annotate('Title', xy=(np.pi, 1.25), fontsize=8.5,
            color=RED, fontweight='bold', ha='center')
ax.annotate('Axes\nlabel', xy=(-0.7, 0), fontsize=7.5,
            color=ACCENT_PURP, fontweight='bold', ha='center')
ax.annotate('Artist\n(scatter)', xy=(1, 0.9), xytext=(2.2, 1.15),
            fontsize=7.5, color=GRAY_DARK,
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=GRAY_DARK, lw=1))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::
::::::

## Building a Plot: Step 1 — Create the Canvas

**Start with a Figure and Axes:**
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Create the canvas: 1 figure with 1 axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))

# ax is now ready to receive data
```

**What this creates:**
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.set_title('Step 1: Empty canvas — figure + axes created', fontsize=12)
ax.set_xlabel('X axis'); ax.set_ylabel('Y axis')
ax.text(0.5, 0.5, 'No data yet', transform=ax.transAxes,
        ha='center', va='center', fontsize=14, color='lightgray')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

**Result:** An empty canvas with labelled axes — we've told matplotlib *how big* but not *what* to draw.

```{=html}
<!-- slide 15 -->
```

## Building a Plot: Step 2 — Add Data

**Plot points with `ax.scatter()`:**
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.normal(0, 1, 100)
y = 0.8 * x + np.random.normal(0, 0.5, 100)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
ax.scatter(x, y)   # Add the data!
plt.show()
```

**What this creates:**
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.normal(0, 1, 100)
y = 0.8 * x + np.random.normal(0, 0.5, 100)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.scatter(x, y)
ax.set_title('Step 2: Data appears as points', fontsize=12)
ax.set_xlabel('X'); ax.set_ylabel('Y')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

**Result:** Points appear — default blue color, default size.

## Building a Plot: Step 3 — Add Color

**Color by group using a loop or seaborn:**
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

np.random.seed(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'x': np.random.normal(0, 1, 100),
    'y': np.random.normal(0, 1, 100),
    'group': np.random.choice(['Control', 'Treatment'], 100)
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
for group, color in zip(['Control', 'Treatment'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW]):
    sub = df[df['group'] == group]
    ax.scatter(sub['x'], sub['y'], label=group, color=color, s=60, alpha=0.7)
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

**What this creates:**
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8

np.random.seed(42)
```

## Building a Plot: Step 4 — Polish & Labels

**Add titles, labels, and trend line:**
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

from scipy.stats import linregress

slope, intercept, *_ = linregress(df['x'], df['y'])
xs = np.linspace(df['x'].min(), df['x'].max(), 100)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
for group, color in zip(['Control', 'Treatment'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW]):
    sub = df[df['group'] == group]
    ax.scatter(sub['x'], sub['y'], label=group, color=color, s=60, alpha=0.7)
ax.plot(xs, slope * xs + intercept, color='black', linewidth=1.5, ls='--')
ax.set_xlabel('Log2 Fold Change', labelpad=8)
ax.set_ylabel('Expression Level', labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('Gene Expression: Control vs Treatment')
ax.legend(title='Group', loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{=html}
<!-- slide 18 -->
```

## Building a Plot: Step 5 — Publication Style

**Set a clean, consistent style for the whole course:**
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

def course_style(ax, title='', xlabel='', ylabel=''):
    """Apply consistent course theme to an axes."""
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, fontsize=11, labelpad=8)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=11, labelpad=8)
    ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5, color='#e0e0e0')
    ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=10)
    return ax
```

## Common Plot Types in Matplotlib & Seaborn

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5

np.random.seed(42)
cats  = ['A','B','C','D']
vals  = [23, 45, 31, 58]
x_sc  = np.random.normal(0, 1, 150)
y_sc  = 0.7*x_sc + np.random.normal(0, 0.6, 150)
g_sc  = np.random.choice(['Ctrl','Treat'], 150)
ts    = np.arange(50)
tsv   = np.cumsum(np.random.normal(0.2, 1, 50))
bx    = [np.random.normal(m, 1.2, 60) for m in [3, 5, 4, 6]]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(12, 5.5), constrained_layout=True)

# Bar
axes[0,0].bar(cats, vals, color=[BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_PURP])
axes[0,0].set_title('ax.bar()\nComparisons', fontsize=9)

# Scatter
for g, c in zip(['Ctrl','Treat'], [BRAND, RED]):
    m = g_sc == g
    axes[0,1].scatter(x_sc[m], y_sc[m], color=c, s=18, alpha=0.6, label=g)
axes[0,1].legend(fontsize=7); axes[0,1].set_title('ax.scatter()\nRelationships', fontsize=9)

# Line
axes[0,2].plot(ts, tsv, color=BRAND, linewidth=2)
axes[0,2].fill_between(ts, tsv, alpha=0.15, color=BRAND)
axes[0,2].set_title('ax.plot()\nTime series', fontsize=9)

# Hist
axes[0,3].hist(np.random.normal(50, 10, 500), bins=25, color=BRAND, alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
axes[0,3].set_title('ax.hist()\nDistributions', fontsize=9)

# Box
bp = axes[1,0].boxplot(bx, patch_artist=True, medianprops={'color':'white','linewidth':2})
for patch, c in zip(bp['boxes'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_PURP]):
    patch.set_facecolor(c); patch.set_alpha(0.7)
axes[1,0].set_title('ax.boxplot()\nDistributions', fontsize=9)

# Heatmap (seaborn)
mat = np.random.randn(8, 8)
sns.heatmap(mat, ax=axes[1,1], cmap='RdYlGn', center=0, linewidths=0.3,
            cbar_kws={'shrink': 0.7})
axes[1,1].set_title('sns.heatmap()\nExpression', fontsize=9)

# Violin
vp = axes[1,2].violinplot(bx, showmedians=True)
for pc, c in zip(vp['bodies'], [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, BRAND_LIGHT, ACCENT_PURP]):
    pc.set_facecolor(c); pc.set_alpha(0.7)
axes[1,2].set_title('ax.violinplot()\nDensity', fontsize=9)

# Pairplot placeholder
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
axes[1,3].add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((0.05,0.05), 0.9, 0.9,
                    boxstyle='round', facecolor=BRAND+'22', edgecolor=BRAND))
axes[1,3].text(0.5, 0.5, 'sns.pairplot()\nMultivariate', ha='center', va='center',
               fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color=BRAND, transform=axes[1,3].transAxes)
axes[1,3].set_xlim(0,1); axes[1,3].set_ylim(0,1); axes[1,3].axis('off')

for ax in axes.flat:
    ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

plt.suptitle('Common Plot Types', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```

# Volcano Plots {background-color="#28A87D"}

```{=html}
<!-- slide 23 -->
```

## What is a Volcano Plot?

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="48%"}
**Purpose:** Visualize differential expression results — identify statistically significant and biologically meaningful changes at a glance.

**Axes:**

- **X-axis:** log₂(Fold Change) — magnitude of change
- **Y-axis:** −log₁₀(p-value) — statistical significance

**Quadrants:**

- Top-right → up-regulated, significant
- Top-left → down-regulated, significant
- Bottom → not significant

**Thresholds (typical):**

- |log₂FC| > 1 (2-fold change)
- p-value < 0.05 → −log₁₀(p) > 1.3
::::

::: {.column width="52%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5.5

np.random.seed(42)
n = 2000
log2fc = np.random.normal(0, 1.5, n)
pvals  = np.random.exponential(0.4, n).clip(1e-30, 1)
# add some truly significant genes
sig_idx = np.random.choice(n, 80, replace=False)
log2fc[sig_idx[:40]] += 3
log2fc[sig_idx[40:]] -= 3
pvals[sig_idx] *= 1e-6

neg_log_p = -np.log10(pvals)
colors = np.where((log2fc >  1) & (neg_log_p > 1.3), BRAND,
         np.where((log2fc < -1) & (neg_log_p > 1.3), RED, 'lightgray'))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5.5))
ax.scatter(log2fc, neg_log_p, c=colors, s=12, alpha=0.7, linewidths=0)
ax.axhline(1.3, color='black', linewidth=0.8, linestyle='--')
ax.axvline( 1,  color='black', linewidth=0.8, linestyle='--')
ax.axvline(-1,  color='black', linewidth=0.8, linestyle='--')
ax.set_xlabel('log₂(Fold Change)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('−log₁₀(p-value)',   fontsize=11)
ax.set_title('Volcano Plot', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
up   = ((log2fc >  1) & (neg_log_p > 1.3)).sum()
down = ((log2fc < -1) & (neg_log_p > 1.3)).sum()
ax.text( 4, neg_log_p.max()*0.92, f'↑ {up}',  color=BRAND, fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax.text(-6, neg_log_p.max()*0.92, f'↓ {down}', color=RED,   fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
:::
::::::

```{=html}
<!-- slide 24 -->
```

## Volcano Plot: Data Preparation

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-10|12-18|20-27"

# Step 1: Generate differential expression results
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

np.random.seed(42)
n_genes = 2000

de_results = pd.DataFrame({
    'gene'    : [f'gene_{i:04d}' for i in range(n_genes)],
    'log2FC'  : np.random.normal(0, 1.5, n_genes),
    'pvalue'  : np.random.exponential(0.4, n_genes).clip(1e-30, 1),
})

# Step 2: Compute derived columns
de_results['neg_log10_p'] = -np.log10(de_results['pvalue'])
de_results['regulation']  = 'ns'   # not significant

up   = (de_results['log2FC'] >  1) & (de_results['neg_log10_p'] > 1.3)
down = (de_results['log2FC'] < -1) & (de_results['neg_log10_p'] > 1.3)
de_results.loc[up,   'regulation'] = 'up'
de_results.loc[down, 'regulation'] = 'down'

# Step 3: Inspect
print(de_results['regulation'].value_counts())
# up       38
# down     41
# ns     1921
```

## Volcano Plot: Building the Figure

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-5|7-17|19-30"

# Color map for regulation status
color_map = {'up': '#28A87D', 'down': '#E74C3C', 'ns': 'lightgray'}
size_map  = {'up': 30,        'down': 30,        'ns': 12}
alpha_map = {'up': 0.85,      'down': 0.85,      'ns': 0.4}

# Build figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6))

for status, group in de_results.groupby('regulation'):
    ax.scatter(group['log2FC'], group['neg_log10_p'],
               c=color_map[status], s=size_map[status],
               alpha=alpha_map[status], label=status,
               linewidths=0, zorder=3 if status != 'ns' else 1)

# Threshold lines
ax.axhline(1.3, color='black', linewidth=0.9, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
ax.axvline( 1,  color='black', linewidth=0.9, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
ax.axvline(-1,  color='black', linewidth=0.9, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Labels & style
ax.set_xlabel('log₂(Fold Change)', fontsize=12, labelpad=8)
ax.set_ylabel('−log₁₀(p-value)',   fontsize=12, labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('Differential Gene Expression', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(title='Regulation', frameon=False)
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Volcano Plot: Labelling Top Genes

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from adjustText import adjust_text   # pip install adjustText

np.random.seed(42)
n = 2000
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'gene'    : [f'gene_{i:04d}' for i in range(n)],
    'log2FC'  : np.random.normal(0, 1.5, n),
    'pvalue'  : np.random.exponential(0.4, n).clip(1e-30, 1),
})
# spike in significant genes
sig = np.random.choice(n, 80, replace=False)
df.loc[sig[:40], 'log2FC'] += 3;  df.loc[sig[40:], 'log2FC'] -= 3
df.loc[sig, 'pvalue'] *= 1e-6
df['neg_log10_p'] = -np.log10(df['pvalue'])
df['reg'] = np.where((df['log2FC']> 1)&(df['neg_log10_p']>1.3),'up',
            np.where((df['log2FC']<-1)&(df['neg_log10_p']>1.3),'down','ns'))

cm = {'up':BRAND,'down':RED,'ns':'lightgray'}
sm = {'up':35,'down':35,'ns':10}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
for st, grp in df.groupby('reg'):
    ax.scatter(grp['log2FC'], grp['neg_log10_p'],
               c=cm[st], s=sm[st], alpha=0.75 if st!='ns' else 0.35,
               linewidths=0, zorder=3 if st!='ns' else 1)
ax.axhline(1.3,color='black',lw=0.9,ls='--',alpha=0.6)
ax.axvline(1,  color='black',lw=0.9,ls='--',alpha=0.6)
ax.axvline(-1, color='black',lw=0.9,ls='--',alpha=0.6)

top = df.nlargest(8,'neg_log10_p')
texts = [ax.text(r['log2FC'], r['neg_log10_p'], r['gene'],
                 fontsize=7, fontweight='bold') for _, r in top.iterrows()]
try:
    adjust_text(texts, ax=ax, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='gray', lw=0.7))
except Exception:
    pass

ax.set_xlabel('log₂(Fold Change)'); ax.set_ylabel('−log₁₀(p-value)')
ax.set_title('Volcano Plot with Top-Gene Labels', fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## PCA, t-SNE and UMAP at a Glance

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5

from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.manifold      import TSNE
from sklearn.datasets      import make_blobs

np.random.seed(42)
X, y = make_blobs(n_samples=400, centers=5, cluster_std=1.8,
                  n_features=50, random_state=42)

pca   = PCA(n_components=2, random_state=42).fit_transform(X)
tsne  = TSNE(n_components=2, random_state=42, perplexity=30).fit_transform(X)

try:
    import umap as umap_lib
    umap_res = umap_lib.UMAP(n_components=2, random_state=42).fit_transform(X)
    has_umap = True
except ImportError:
    has_umap = False

palette = [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, ACCENT_PURP, RED, '#3498DB']
labels  = ['Cluster A','Cluster B','Cluster C','Cluster D','Cluster E']

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3 if has_umap else 2, figsize=(11, 4.5))

for ax, coords, title in zip(
    axes,
    [pca, tsne] + ([umap_res] if has_umap else []),
    ['PCA', 't-SNE', 'UMAP'] if has_umap else ['PCA', 't-SNE']
):
    for i, (lab, col) in enumerate(zip(labels, palette)):
        m = y == i
        ax.scatter(coords[m,0], coords[m,1], color=col, s=20,
                   alpha=0.75, label=lab, linewidths=0)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Component 1'); ax.set_ylabel('Component 2')
    ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

axes[0].legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc='upper left')
plt.suptitle('Dimensionality Reduction Comparison (50D → 2D)',
             fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

| Method | Preserves | Speed | Main use |
|--------|-----------|-------|----------|
| **PCA** | Global variance | Fast | Quick QC, linear structure |
| **t-SNE** | Local clusters | Medium | Cluster visualization |
| **UMAP** | Local + some global | Fast | Single-cell, large datasets |

## PCA: Step-by-Step Code

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-8|10-14|16-28"

# Step 1: Prepare gene expression matrix (genes × samples → samples × genes)
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

np.random.seed(42)
# 200 samples × 5 000 genes (simulated RNA-seq log2-counts)
X = np.random.normal(8, 2, (200, 5000))
groups = np.repeat(['Control', 'Treatment'], 100)

# Step 2: Scale and run PCA
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

pca = PCA(n_components=10, random_state=42)
coords = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)  # shape: (200, 10)
var_explained = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100

# Step 3: Plot PC1 vs PC2
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
for grp, color in zip(['Control', 'Treatment'], ['#28A87D', '#E8A838']):
    m = groups == grp
    ax.scatter(coords[m, 0], coords[m, 1], color=color,
               s=50, alpha=0.75, label=grp, linewidths=0)
ax.set_xlabel(f'PC1 ({var_explained[0]:.1f}%)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel(f'PC2 ({var_explained[1]:.1f}%)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_title('PCA of RNA-seq Data', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(title='Group', frameon=False)
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## PCA: Scree Plot & Variance Explained

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

np.random.seed(42)
X = np.random.normal(8, 2, (200, 5000))
X_scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
pca = PCA(n_components=20, random_state=42).fit(X_scaled)
var = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
cum = np.cumsum(var)

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 5))

# Scree plot
ax1.bar(range(1, 21), var, color=BRAND, alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
ax1.set_xlabel('Principal Component'); ax1.set_ylabel('Variance Explained (%)')
ax1.set_title('Scree Plot', fontweight='bold')
ax1.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

# Cumulative variance
ax2.plot(range(1, 21), cum, marker='o', color=BRAND,
         markersize=6, linewidth=2)
ax2.axhline(80, color=RED, linewidth=1, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7, label='80% threshold')
ax2.fill_between(range(1, 21), cum, alpha=0.15, color=BRAND)
ax2.set_xlabel('Number of PCs'); ax2.set_ylabel('Cumulative Variance (%)')
ax2.set_title('Cumulative Variance', fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(frameon=False); ax2.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## t-SNE: Theory

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="55%"}
**t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding)**

Converts high-dimensional distances into probabilities, then places points in 2D so that *similar* points are neighbours.

**Key parameters:**

| Parameter | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| `perplexity` (5–50) | Controls effective number of neighbours; higher → more global structure |
| `n_iter` (≥ 1000) | More iterations → better convergence |
| `learning_rate` | Typical range 10–1000 |

**When to use:**

✅ Revealing cluster structure in single-cell data
✅ Comparing transcriptional states
⚠️ Distances between clusters are **not** meaningful
⚠️ Run on PCA-reduced data (50 PCs) for speed
::::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: fragment
**Typical workflow:**
```python
# Correct approach
pca50 = PCA(n_components=50)
X_pca = pca50.fit_transform(X_scaled)

tsne = TSNE(perplexity=30, n_iter=1000)
embedding = tsne.fit_transform(X_pca)
```
:::

::: fragment
**Common mistake:**
```python
# Wrong – running t-SNE on raw 5000-gene matrix
# is very slow and noisy
tsne.fit_transform(X_raw)   # ❌
```
:::
:::
::::::

```{=html}
<!-- slide 31b -->
```

## t-SNE: Code Walkthrough

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-6|8-13|15-28"

# Step 1: Start from PCA-reduced data (recommended for speed)
from sklearn.manifold import TSNE

# Use top 50 PCs as input to t-SNE
pca50 = PCA(n_components=50, random_state=42)
X_pca50 = pca50.fit_transform(X_scaled)

# Step 2: Run t-SNE
tsne = TSNE(
    n_components = 2,
    perplexity   = 30,      # typical range: 5–50
    n_iter       = 1000,
    random_state = 42,
)
coords_tsne = tsne.fit_transform(X_pca50)

# Step 3: Plot with cell-type annotations
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
for cell, color in zip(cell_types, COURSE_PAL):
    m = annotations == cell
    ax.scatter(coords_tsne[m,0], coords_tsne[m,1],
               color=color, s=20, alpha=0.8, label=cell, linewidths=0)

ax.set_xlabel('t-SNE 1'); ax.set_ylabel('t-SNE 2')
ax.set_title('t-SNE: Single-Cell RNA-seq', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(title='Cell type', fontsize=8, frameon=False,
          bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), loc='upper left')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

::: {.footer style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #606060;"}
**Tip:** Always run t-SNE on PCA-reduced data for reproducibility and speed on large datasets.
:::

```{=html}
<!-- slide 33 -->
```

## UMAP: Theory

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="55%"}
**UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection)**

Constructs a topological representation of the data and optimises a low-dimensional layout that best preserves both local *and* some global structure.

**Key parameters:**

| Parameter | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| `n_neighbors` (5–200) | Low → fine local detail; high → more global |
| `min_dist` (0.0–0.99) | Low → tight clusters; high → spread out |
| `metric` | Distance metric (`'euclidean'`, `'cosine'`, …) |

**Comparison with t-SNE:**

| Feature | t-SNE | UMAP |
|---------|-------|------|
| Speed | Slower | Faster |
| Global structure | ✗ | Some |
| Reproducibility | ✗ | ✅ (with seed) |
| Out-of-sample | ✗ | ✅ |

::::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: fragment
```python
import umap

# UMAP preserves more global structure
# and is faster than t-SNE on large datasets
reducer = umap.UMAP(
    n_neighbors  = 15,
    min_dist     = 0.1,
    n_components = 2,
    random_state = 42,
)
embedding = reducer.fit_transform(X_pca50)
```
:::

::: fragment
**UMAP is the default for single-cell analysis:**
```python
# scanpy (single-cell analysis toolkit)
import scanpy as sc
sc.tl.umap(adata)
sc.pl.umap(adata, color='cell_type')
```
:::
:::
::::::

```{=html}
<!-- slide 32b -->
```

```{python}

    n_neighbors  = 15,    # balances local/global structure
```

Analyse this simulated single-cell RNA-seq dataset:
```{python}
#| echo: true

np.random.seed(2026)
n_cells, n_genes = 800, 3000

# 4 cell types with distinct expression profiles
cell_types = np.repeat(['T_cell','B_cell','NK_cell','Monocyte'], 200)
centers = {
    'T_cell'   : np.random.normal(8.0, 0.3, n_genes),

# Your tasks:
# 1. Scale X_sc with StandardScaler
```

## Heatmap Fundamentals

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="48%"}
**What heatmaps show:**

- Gene × sample expression matrices
- Correlation matrices
- Presence/absence patterns
- Epigenomic signals (ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq)

**Key features:**

- Color encodes value (sequential or diverging palette)
- Hierarchical clustering groups similar rows/columns
- Dendrograms reveal sample relationships
- Annotations add metadata (condition, batch, etc.)

**Libraries:**

- `seaborn.clustermap` — quick, good defaults
- `PyComplexHeatmap` — publication-quality with rich annotations
::::

::: {.column width="52%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5.5

np.random.seed(42)
n_genes, n_samples = 30, 20

# Two-group structure
base  = np.random.normal(0, 1, (n_genes, n_samples))
base[:15, :10] += 2.5   # up in group 1
base[15:, 10:] += 2.5   # up in group 2

df_heat = pd.DataFrame(
    base,
    index   = [f'Gene{i:03d}' for i in range(n_genes)],
    columns = [f'S{i:02d}' for i in range(n_samples)],
)

cg = sns.clustermap(
    df_heat, cmap='RdBu_r', center=0,
    figsize=(6, 5.5), linewidths=0,
    xticklabels=False, yticklabels=False,
    cbar_kws={'label': 'z-score'},
)
cg.ax_heatmap.set_xlabel('Samples'); cg.ax_heatmap.set_ylabel('Genes')
plt.show()
```
:::
::::::

```{=html}
<!-- slide 37 -->
```

## Seaborn Clustermap: Code

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-9|11-18|20-32"

# Step 1: Prepare expression matrix
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import zscore

np.random.seed(42)
expr_matrix = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.normal(8, 2, (50, 24)),
    index   = [f'Gene_{i:03d}' for i in range(50)],
    columns = [f'S{i:02d}'     for i in range(24)],
)

# Step 2: Z-score normalize (per gene)
expr_z = expr_matrix.apply(zscore, axis=1)

# Sample annotation for color bar
groups = pd.Series(
    ['Control'] * 12 + ['Treatment'] * 12,
    index=expr_matrix.columns
)
col_colors = groups.map({'Control': '#28A87D', 'Treatment': '#E8A838'})

# Step 3: Build the clustermap
cg = sns.clustermap(
    expr_z,
    cmap        = 'RdBu_r',
    center      = 0,
    col_colors  = col_colors,      # annotation bar on top
    row_cluster = True,
    col_cluster = True,
    figsize     = (10, 8),
    linewidths  = 0,
    cbar_kws    = {'label': 'z-score', 'shrink': 0.5},
)
cg.fig.suptitle('Gene Expression Heatmap', y=1.02,
                fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
plt.show()
```

## PyComplexHeatmap: Rich Annotations

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-4|6-15|17-30"

# pip install PyComplexHeatmap
from PyComplexHeatmap import ClusterMapPlotter, anno_label, anno_barplot

# Step 1: Build annotation DataFrames
sample_anno = pd.DataFrame({
    'Condition' : ['Control'] * 12 + ['Treated'] * 12,
    'Batch'     : list('AABBCCAABBCC') * 2,
    'QC_score'  : np.random.uniform(0.85, 1.0, 24),
}, index=expr_matrix.columns)

gene_anno = pd.DataFrame({
    'Pathway' : np.random.choice(
        ['Apoptosis','Cell cycle','Metabolism','Signaling'], 50),
    'mean_exp': expr_matrix.mean(axis=1),
}, index=expr_matrix.index)

# Step 2: Plot with full annotation suite
col_ha = HeatmapAnnotation(
    Condition = anno_simple(sample_anno['Condition'],
                            colors={'Control':'#28A87D','Treated':'#E8A838'}),
    Batch     = anno_simple(sample_anno['Batch']),
    QC        = anno_barplot(sample_anno['QC_score'], height=15,
                             colors='#28A87D'),
)

cm = ClusterMapPlotter(
    data        = expr_z,
    top_annotation = col_ha,
    cmap        = 'RdBu_r',
    row_cluster = True,
    col_cluster = True,
    label       = 'z-score',
    figsize     = (12, 9),
)
```

## Waffle Charts: Proportions at a Glance

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="48%"}
**Purpose:** Show part-to-whole relationships as a grid of squares — more intuitive than pie charts for proportions.

**When to use:**

- Sample composition (cell types, genotypes)
- Cohort demographics
- Variant classification counts
- Any whole-number percentage summary

**Library:** `PyWaffle`
```bash
pip install pywaffle
```

## Waterfall Plots: Mutation Landscapes

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="48%"}
**Purpose:** Display somatic mutation burden across a patient cohort — a staple of cancer genomics papers.

**What the plot shows:**

- Each bar = one patient, height = tumor mutation burden (TMB)
- Bars sorted by TMB (descending)
- Color can encode cancer subtype, treatment response, or driver mutation
- Often paired with an **OncoPrint** (mutation matrix below)
::::

::: {.column width="52%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

np.random.seed(42)
n_patients = 60
tmb = np.sort(np.random.lognormal(3, 1.2, n_patients))[::-1]
subtypes = np.random.choice(['Luminal A','Luminal B','HER2+','TNBC'], n_patients)
color_map_st = {'Luminal A': BRAND, 'Luminal B': ACCENT_YLW,
                'HER2+': ACCENT_PURP, 'TNBC': RED}
colors = [color_map_st[s] for s in subtypes]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
ax.bar(range(n_patients), tmb, color=colors, width=1.0, edgecolor='none')
ax.set_xlabel('Patient (sorted by TMB)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Tumor Mutation Burden\n(mutations / Mb)', fontsize=10)
ax.set_title('Waterfall Plot: Mutation Burden', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
ax.set_xticks([])

from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=c, label=l)
                   for l, c in color_map_st.items()]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, fontsize=8, frameon=False,
          loc='upper right')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
:::
::::::

```{=html}
<!-- slide 44 -->
```

## Waterfall Plot: Code

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-11|13-23|25-35"

# Step 1: Simulate TMB data
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

np.random.seed(42)
n = 80
patients = pd.DataFrame({
    'patient'  : [f'P{i:03d}' for i in range(n)],
    'TMB'      : np.random.lognormal(3, 1.2, n),
    'subtype'  : np.random.choice(['Luminal A','Luminal B','HER2+','TNBC'], n),
    'response' : np.random.choice(['CR','PR','SD','PD'], n,
                                  p=[0.15, 0.35, 0.30, 0.20]),
})

# Step 2: Sort and assign colors
patients = patients.sort_values('TMB', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
color_map = {'Luminal A':'#28A87D','Luminal B':'#E8A838',
             'HER2+':'#7754BF','TNBC':'#E74C3C'}
colors = patients['subtype'].map(color_map)

# Step 3: Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
ax.bar(range(n), patients['TMB'], color=colors, width=1.0, edgecolor='none')
ax.set_yscale('log')   # log scale common for TMB
ax.set_xlabel('Patient (sorted by TMB)', fontsize=12, labelpad=8)
ax.set_ylabel('Tumor Mutation Burden (log scale)', fontsize=12, labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('Somatic Mutation Landscape', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
ax.set_xticks([])
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=c, label=l) for l, c in color_map.items()]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, frameon=False, loc='upper right')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## What Are Genomic Peaks?

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
**Peaks** are genomic regions with elevated signal in assays such as:

- **ChIP-seq** — transcription factor binding sites, histone marks
- **ATAC-seq** — open chromatin regions
- **Cut&Run / CUT&TAG** — protein–DNA interactions

**Key visualization goals:**

- Show signal track across a genomic region
- Compare peaks between conditions
- Overlay gene annotations
- Display multiple marks simultaneously

**Tools in Python:**

- `pyGenomeTracks` — multi-track genome browser plots
- `pysam` + `matplotlib` — custom signal plots
- `dna_features_viewer` — gene / feature maps
::::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5.5

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(6, 5.5),
                         sharex=True, gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3,3,3,1]})
np.random.seed(42)
x = np.linspace(0, 10000, 500)

def peak_signal(centers, width=400, noise=0.15):
    s = noise * np.random.randn(len(x))
    for c in centers:
        s += np.exp(-((x - c)**2) / (2 * width**2)) * np.random.uniform(0.7, 1.3)
    return np.clip(s, 0, None)

s1 = peak_signal([2500, 5000, 7800])
s2 = peak_signal([2500, 7800])
s3 = peak_signal([5000])

axes[0].fill_between(x, s1, color=BRAND,    alpha=0.8)
axes[0].set_ylabel('H3K27ac', fontsize=8, labelpad=2)
axes[0].spines[['top','right','bottom']].set_visible(False)

axes[1].fill_between(x, s2, color=ACCENT_PURP, alpha=0.8)
axes[1].set_ylabel('H3K4me3', fontsize=8, labelpad=2)
axes[1].spines[['top','right','bottom']].set_visible(False)

axes[2].fill_between(x, s3, color=ACCENT_YLW, alpha=0.8)
axes[2].set_ylabel('ATAC-seq', fontsize=8, labelpad=2)
axes[2].spines[['top','right','bottom']].set_visible(False)

# Gene track
for gene_x, gene_len, strand, name in [
    (1500, 2000, '+', 'GeneA'), (5500, 3000, '-', 'GeneB')
]:
    ax = axes[3]
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((gene_x, 0.3), gene_len, 0.4,
                                color=GRAY_DARK, alpha=0.7))
    ax.text(gene_x + gene_len/2, 0.5, name, ha='center', va='center',
            fontsize=7, color='white', fontweight='bold')
axes[3].set_ylim(0, 1); axes[3].set_ylabel('Genes', fontsize=8, labelpad=2)
axes[3].spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
axes[3].set_xlabel('Genomic position (bp)', fontsize=9)

fig.suptitle('Multi-Track Genome Browser', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
:::

```{python}
[bigwig track]
file = H3K27ac.bw
height = 3

title = H3K27ac

[spacer]
height = 0.3

[bigwig track 2]
file = ATAC.bw
height = 3
color = #7754BF
title = ATAC-seq

[genes]
file = genes.gtf
height = 1.5
title = Genes
"""

with open('tracks.ini', 'w') as f:
```

## Custom Peak Plot with Matplotlib

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.linspace(0, 10000, 500)

def make_track(centers, noise=0.08):
    s = noise * np.abs(np.random.randn(len(x)))
    for c in centers:
        s += np.exp(-((x - c)**2) / (2 * 300**2)) * np.random.uniform(0.9, 1.1)
    return np.clip(s, 0, None)

tracks = {
    'H3K27ac (active enhancer)' : (make_track([2500, 5100, 7800]), BRAND),
    'H3K4me3 (active promoter)' : (make_track([2500, 7800]),        ACCENT_PURP),
    'ATAC-seq (open chromatin)' : (make_track([2500, 5100, 7800]), ACCENT_YLW),
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    len(tracks) + 1, 1, figsize=(10, 5.5), sharex=True,
    gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 3, 3, 1.2]},
)

for ax, (label, (signal, color)) in zip(axes, tracks.items()):
    ax.fill_between(x, signal, color=color, alpha=0.85)
    ax.set_ylabel(label, fontsize=8, labelpad=4)
    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0); ax.spines[['top','right','bottom']].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)

# Gene annotation track
gene_ax = axes[-1]
for start, length, name in [(1200,2200,'GeneA'),(5800,2800,'GeneB')]:
    gene_ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((start, 0.25), length, 0.5,
                                     color=GRAY_DARK, alpha=0.8, clip_on=False))
    gene_ax.text(start + length/2, 0.5, name, ha='center', va='center',
                 fontsize=7, color='white', fontweight='bold')
gene_ax.set_ylim(0, 1); gene_ax.set_ylabel('Genes', fontsize=8)
gene_ax.set_xlabel('Genomic position (bp)', fontsize=10, labelpad=8)
gene_ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)

fig.suptitle('Epigenomic Signal Tracks — chr1:0-10 kb', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Exercise: Peak Visualization

::: {.question}
**Coding Exercise**

Build a multi-track genome browser plot from scratch:
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

np.random.seed(2026)
region_size = 20000          # 20 kb window
x = np.linspace(0, region_size, 1000)

def simulate_signal(peak_centers, peak_width=500, noise=0.05):
    """Return a ChIP/ATAC-like signal track."""
    s = noise * np.abs(np.random.randn(len(x)))
    for c in peak_centers:
        height = np.random.uniform(0.7, 1.5)
        s += height * np.exp(-((x - c)**2) / (2 * peak_width**2))
    return np.clip(s, 0, None)

tracks = {
    'H3K27ac'   : simulate_signal([3000, 8500, 15000]),
    'H3K4me3'   : simulate_signal([3000, 15000]),
    'CTCF'      : simulate_signal([8500, 12000]),
    'ATAC-seq'  : simulate_signal([3000, 8500, 12000, 15000], peak_width=300),
}

genes = pd.DataFrame({
    'name'  : ['GeneA', 'GeneB', 'GeneC'],
    'start' : [1500,     7000,    13500],
    'end'   : [4500,    10500,   17000],
    'strand': ['+',      '-',     '+'],
})

# Your tasks:
# 1. Plot each track in a separate subplot sharing the x-axis
# 2. Fill the area under each signal curve with a distinct color
# 3. Draw the gene annotation track at the bottom
#    - Use rectangles for gene bodies
#    - Add strand arrows (→ for +, ← for –)
#    - Label gene names
# 4. Add a vertical shaded region at a shared peak (e.g. 8200–8800 bp)
# 5. Polish: y-axis labels, shared x-axis label, overall title

# Bonus: Use pyGenomeTracks to replicate the same plot from an INI config
```

## Gene Ontology & Pathway Enrichment

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
**What enrichment analysis shows:**

- Which biological processes are over-represented in a gene list
- GO terms: Biological Process, Molecular Function, Cellular Component
- KEGG / Reactome pathways

**Typical workflow:**

1. Run differential expression
2. Select significant genes (up / down)
3. Test for pathway over-representation
4. Visualize top enriched pathways

**Python tools:**

- `gget enrichr` — simple API to Enrichr database
- `gprofiler-official` — g:Profiler API
- `gseapy` — GSEA and over-representation analysis
::::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 5.5

pathways = [
    'Cell division', 'DNA replication', 'DNA repair',
    'Apoptosis', 'p53 signaling', 'Notch signaling',
    'Wnt signaling', 'mTOR pathway', 'MAPK cascade',
    'Cell migration',
]
enrichment = -np.log10(np.random.uniform(1e-15, 0.04, 10))
gene_count = np.random.randint(10, 120, 10)
enrichment_sorted = np.argsort(enrichment)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 5.5))
bars = ax.barh(
    range(10), enrichment[enrichment_sorted],
    color=[BRAND if v > 5 else BRAND_LIGHT for v in enrichment[enrichment_sorted]],
    alpha=0.85, edgecolor='none',
)
ax.set_yticks(range(10))
ax.set_yticklabels([pathways[i] for i in enrichment_sorted], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xlabel('−log₁₀(adjusted p-value)', fontsize=10)
ax.set_title('Top Enriched Pathways', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(x=-np.log10(0.05), color=RED, linewidth=1.2, linestyle='--',
           alpha=0.7, label='p = 0.05')
ax.legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False)
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## gget: Enrichment in One Line

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-3|5-11|13-28"

# pip install gget
import gget
gget.setup('enrichr')   # one-time setup

# Step 1: Run enrichment on a gene list
gene_list = [
    'TP53','BRCA1','BRCA2','CDKN1A','MDM2','BAX',
    'BCL2','CASP3','CASP9','ATM','CHEK2','PTEN',
    'RB1','E2F1','CDK2','CCND1','MYC','EGFR',
]
results = gget.enrichr(
    genes    = gene_list,
    database = 'KEGG_2021_Human',
    plot     = False,
)

# Step 2: Visualize top 10 enriched pathways
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

top10 = results.head(10).sort_values('adj_p_val')
neg_log_p = -np.log10(top10['adj_p_val'])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
bars = ax.barh(range(len(top10)), neg_log_p,
               color=[BRAND if p < 0.01 else BRAND_LIGHT
                      for p in top10['adj_p_val']],
               alpha=0.85, edgecolor='none')
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top10)))
ax.set_yticklabels(top10['pathway'], fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel('−log₁₀(adjusted p-value)', fontsize=11, labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('KEGG Pathway Enrichment', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.axvline(-np.log10(0.05), color=RED, lw=1.2, ls='--', label='p = 0.05')
ax.legend(frameon=False); ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Bubble Plot: Enrichment with Gene Counts

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

np.random.seed(2026)

pathways_data = pd.DataFrame({
    'pathway'    : [
        'Cell division', 'DNA replication', 'DNA repair',
        'Apoptosis', 'p53 signaling', 'Notch signaling',
        'Wnt signaling', 'mTOR pathway', 'MAPK cascade', 'Cell migration',
    ],
    'neg_log10_p': np.random.uniform(2, 12, 10),
    'gene_count' : np.random.randint(10, 120, 10),
    'gene_ratio' : np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.6, 10),
    'category'   : np.random.choice(
        ['Cell cycle','DNA processes','Signaling','Cell motility'], 10),
})
pathways_data = pathways_data.sort_values('neg_log10_p', ascending=True)

cat_colors = {'Cell cycle': BRAND, 'DNA processes': ACCENT_PURP,
              'Signaling': ACCENT_YLW, 'Cell motility': RED}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
for _, row in pathways_data.iterrows():
    ax.scatter(row['gene_ratio'], row['pathway'],
               s=row['gene_count'] * 3,
               c=cat_colors[row['category']],
               alpha=0.8, zorder=3)
    ax.text(row['gene_ratio'] + 0.01, row['pathway'],
            f"  p={10**(-row['neg_log10_p']):.1e}",
            va='center', fontsize=7.5, color=GRAY_DARK)

from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0],[0], marker='o', color='w', markersize=8,
                           markerfacecolor=c, label=l, alpha=0.85)
                   for l, c in cat_colors.items()]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, title='Category', fontsize=8,
          frameon=False, loc='lower right')
ax.set_xlabel('Gene Ratio (genes hit / pathway size)', fontsize=11, labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('Pathway Enrichment Bubble Plot', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
    'direction' : 'down',
})

enrichment_results = pd.concat([pathways_up, pathways_down])
```

## What We Covered Today

::: {.recap}
**Python visualization ecosystem**

- matplotlib (figure anatomy, building plots step by step)

- plotly (interactive counterparts)

::: fragment
::: {.recap}
**Genomics plot types**

| Plot | Library | Use case |
|------|---------|----------|
| Volcano | matplotlib / DashBio | Differential expression |
| PCA / t-SNE / UMAP | scikit-learn | Dimensionality reduction |
| Heatmap | seaborn / PyComplexHeatmap | Expression matrices |
| Waffle | PyWaffle | Proportions |
| Waterfall | matplotlib | Mutation burden |
| Peaks | pyGenomeTracks / matplotlib | ChIP-seq / ATAC-seq |
| Pathway | gget / gseapy | Enrichment results |
:::
